newsitem.title: DUBAI: Attiyah remains Qatar oil minister in reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Attiyah remains Qatar oil minister in reshuffle.

text.p: Abdullah Bin Hamad Al Attiyah has kept his position as Qatar's Minister for Energy and Industry during a cabinet reshuffle, an official decree issued by the country's emir said on Wednesday.
Diplomatic sources in Doha had expected the creation of a new Supreme Energy Council to replace Attiyah's ministry of energy and industry at the same time as the naming of the new cabinet.
The sources said the Council could still be created before the end of this year.
Attiyah has been Qatar's energy and industry minister since September 1992 and has steered a government policy that has seen unprecedented investment in the state's gas and oil sector.
At the last OPEC ministerial meeting in Vienna in June Attiyah, a history graduate, was the second-longest serving minister after Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh.
Qatar's oil production stands close to 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) and it will start exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Japan in December.
Qatar's foreign, finance, defence and interior ministers also retained their positions in Wednesday's reshuffle.
